surface of the Earth and Mars as $10ms^{- 2}$ and $4ms^{- 2}$, respectively. Identify from the below figures, the curve that fits best for the weight of the passenger as a function of time.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the passenger moves away from the Earth at some point, gravitational force due to earth will be minimised and then start increasing as the passenger moves towards& Mars as& $g ∝ \dfrac{1}{R2}$also gravitational force cannot be negative.~Therefore, the correct curve that fits best for the weight of the passenger as a function of time is~ \left(c\right)$.

questions.q: The height of any point $P$ above the surface of earth is equal to diameter of earth. The value of acceleration due to gravity at point $P$ will be : (Given $g =$acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ from the surface of the Earth,
$g^{'} = g\dfrac{1}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)2}$
Given:~$h = 2R$
$∴ g^{'} = g\dfrac{1}{\left(1 + 2\right)2}$
or~$g^{'} = \dfrac{g}{9}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If$E$be the total energy of a satellite moving around the earth, then its potential energy will be~$\dfrac{E}{2}$.

Statement II: The kinetic energy of a satellite revolving in an orbit is equal to the half the magnitude of total energy $E$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

$\begin{cases}W & = & Fx \\ & = & ∆ KE\end{cases}$

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that~they have the same displacement, i.e.,~${x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

questions.q: A light planet is revolving around a massive star in a circular orbit of radius $R$ with a period of revolution $T .$ If the force of attraction between planet and star is proportional to $R^{- 3 / 2}$ then choose the correct option :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the gravitational force of attraction be $F = \dfrac{GMm}{R3 / 2}$.

Now, this gravitational force will provide the required centripetal force. Therefore,

$\dfrac{GMm}{R3 / 2} = m{ω}^{2}R$

$⇒ {ω}^{2} ∝ \dfrac{1}{R5 / 2} ∵ T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω}$

$⇒ T^{2} ∝ R^{5 / 2}$

questions.q: Two planets have masses& $M$~and~$16M$~and their radii are a and~$2a$, respectively. The separation between the centres of the planets is~$10a$. A body of mass~$m$& is fired from the surface of the larger planet towards the smaller planet along the line joining their centres. For the body to be able to reach at the surface of smaller planet, the minimum firing speed needed is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}{mu}^{2} + \left[\dfrac{- G \times 10Mm}{2a} - \dfrac{GMm}{8a}\right] = 0 - \dfrac{G \times 16Mm}{8a} - \dfrac{GM \times m}{2a}$

$⇒ u = \sqrt{\dfrac{45GM}{4a}}$

$u = \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{5GM}{a}}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as& Assertion A& and the other is labelled as& Reason R.

Assertion A:& Earth has atmosphere whereas moon doesn’t have any atmosphere.

Reason R:& The escape velocity on moon is very small as compared to that on earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$~is~$NOT$~the correct explanation of $A$
Both& $A$~and~$R$~are correct and~$R$~ is the correct explanation of~$A$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the escape velocity is given by

${v}_{e} = \sqrt{2gR} . . . ( 1 )$

As both the acceleration and radius of the Moon is much less than that of the Earth, the value of the escape velocity in Moon is much less than that on the Earth.

The average velocity of gas molecules remains higher than the escape velocity due to the lower escape velocity on the moon's surface, making the moon unable to maintain an atmosphere.

questions.q: The mass and the diameter of a planet are three times the respective values for the Earth. The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum on the Earth is $2 \mathrm{~s}$. The period of oscillation of the same pendulum on the planet would be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrmR^{2}}\frac{g_{p}}{g_{e}}=\frac{M_{p}}{M_{e}}\left(\frac{R_{e}}{R_{p}}\right)^{2}=3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}=\frac{1}{3}$ Also $\mathrm{T} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{g}}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{p}}}}=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{p}}=2 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~s}$

$

questions.solution:
Let the initial mass of the sphere is $m ' .$ Hence, mass of

questions.q: If the distance of the earth from Sun is $1 . 5 \times {10}^{6}km$,~then the distance of an imaginary planet from Sun, if its period of revolution is $2 . 83$ years is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Kepler's law of periods, we know that

$T^{2} ∝ R^{3} ⇒ \left(\dfrac{T1}{T2}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{R1}{R2}\right)3$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{2 . 83}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{1 . 5 \times {10}^{6}}{R2}\right)3$

$⇒ {R}_{2} = \left[\left(2 . 83\right)2 \times \left(1 . 5 \times {10}^{6}\right)3\right]\dfrac{1}{3}$

$= 8\dfrac{1}{3} \times 1 . 5 \times {10}^{6} = 3 \times {10}^{6}km$

questions.q: A space ship of mass $2 \times {10}^{4}kg$ is launched into a circular orbit close to the earth surface. The additional velocity to be imparted to the space ship in the orbit to overcome the gravitational pull will be (if $g = 10ms^{- 2}$~and radius of earth $= 6400km$ ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
& The orbital velocity of satellite is&

${v}_{orb} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}}$

The escape velocity is~

${v}_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$

Hence, the additional velocity required is~

$\Deltav = {v}_{esc} - {v}_{orb} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} - \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}} = ( \sqrt{2} - 1 ) \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}}$
$= ( \sqrt{2} - 1 ) \sqrt{gR}$
$= ( \sqrt{2} - 1 ) \sqrt{10 \times 6400 \times {10}^{3}}$
$= 8 ( \sqrt{2} - 1 ) kms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two stars of masses $3 \times {10}^{31}kg$ each, and at distance $2 \times {10}^{11}m$ rotate in a plane about their common centre of mass $O .$ A meteorite passes through $O$ moving perpendicular to the stars,s~rotation plane. In order to escape from the gravitational field of this double star, the minimum speed that meteorite should have at $O$ is ( Take Gravitational constant $G = 6.67 \times {10}^{- 11}Nm^{2}{kg}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
To escape, the total energy of small particle must be zero.



$TE = KE + U$

$0 = \dfrac{1}{2}mV^{2} + \left(\dfrac{- GMm}{d2}\right)\times 2$

$⇒ V = \sqrt{\dfrac{8GM}{d}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{8 \times 6.67 \times {10}^{- 11} \times 3 \times {10}^{31}}{2 \times {10}^{11}}}$

$= 2.8 \times {10}^{5}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
The percentage decrease in the weight of a rocket, when taken to a height of $32$ km above the surface of earth will, be
(Radius of earth $= 6400km$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at a height $h < < R$~is

$g^{'} = g \left($1 - $\dfrac{2h}{R}\right)

Now, change in~$g$~is~

$∴ $\dfrac{\Deltag}{g} = \dfrac{2h}{R}

Percentage change is~

$⇒ $\dfrac{\Deltag}{g} \times$100 = $\dfrac{2h}{R} \times$100$

$= 2 $\times \dfrac{32}{6400} \times$100 = 1 %$

$

Hence option (4)

questions.q:
The length of a seconds pendulum at a height $h = 2R$~from earth surface will be:

(Given: $R =$ Radius of earth and acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth $g = {π}^{2}ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at the given height, $g ' = \dfrac{GM}{\left(3R\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{9}\dfrac{GM}{\left(R\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{9}g$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the Earth.

Now, time period is given by, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g '}}$

Also the time period of second pendulum is $2$ sec.

Therefore, $T = 2sec$

Then, $2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g} \times 9}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{9}m$

questions.q: Four identical particles of equal masses $1$ kg made to move along the circumference of a circle of radius $1m$ under the action of their own mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${F}_{1} = \dfrac{Gmm}{\left(2R\right)2} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}$

${F}_{2} = \dfrac{Gmm}{\left(\sqrt{2}R\right)2} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}$

${F}_{3} = \dfrac{Gmm}{\left(\sqrt{2}R\right)2} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}$

$⇒ {F}_{net} = {F}_{1} + {F}_{2}\cos 45 ° + {F}_{3}\cos 45 °$

$= \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}} + \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}\dfrac{1}{2}$

$= \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{R2} \left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}\left($1 + 2$\sqrt{2}\right)

${F}_{net} = $\dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}\left($1 + 2$\sqrt{2}\right) = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}

$⇒ v = \dfrac{G\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}{2}$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The angular speed of the moon in its orbit about the earth is more than the angular speed of the earth in its orbit about the sun.
Reason (R): The moon takes less time to move around the earth than the time taken by the earth to move around the sun.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of A.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of A.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is known that

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} ⇒ \omega ∝ \dfrac{1}{T}$

As,
${T}_{moon} \approx 27$ days
${T}_{earth} \approx 365$ days
$⇒ {ω}_{moon} > {ω}_{earth}$

Hence, Both the assertion and the reason are correct and the reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

questions.q: The energy required to take a satellite to a height h$above the Earth surface (radius of Earth $= 6.4 \times {10}^{3}km$ ) is ${E}_{1}$, and the kinetic energy required for the satellite to be in a circular orbit at this height is ${E}_{2} .$ The value of $h$ for which ${E}_{1}$ and ${E}_{2}$ are equal, is$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${U}_{surface} + {E}_{1} = {U}_{h}$

$KE$ of satellite is zero at earth surface and at height $h$

$- \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{Re} + {E}_{1} = - G{M}_{e}m \left({R}_{e} +h\right)$

${E}_{1} = G{M}_{e}m \left(\dfrac{1}{Re} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{e} + h}\right)$

${E}_{1} = G{M}_{e}m\left({R}_{e} +h\right)\times \dfrac{h}{Re}$

Gravitational attraction ${F}_{G} = m{a}_{C} = mv^{2} \left({R}_{e} +h\right)$

$⇒ mv^{2}\left({R}_{e} +h\right) = $\dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{ \left({R}_{e} +h\right)2}

$mv^{2} = G{M}_{e}m\left({R}_{e} +h\right)$

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{2\left({R}_{e} + h\right)}$

${E}_{1} = {E}_{2}$

$\dfrac{h}{Re} = \dfrac{1}{2}⇒ h = \dfrac{Re}{2} =3200$ km

questions.q: The mass density of a planet of radius R varies with the distance r from its centre as $ρ ( r ) = {ρ}_{0}  \left($1 - \dfrac{r2}{R2}\right)$Then the gravitational field is maximum at:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dm = ρ \times 4{πx}^{2}dx = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{x2}{r2}\right) \times 4{πx}^{2}dx$

$m = 4\pi ρ{∫}_{0}^{r}\left(x^{2} - \dfrac{x4}{R2}\right)dxs$

$m = 4{πρ}_{0}\left|\dfrac{r3}{3} - \dfrac{r5}{5R^{2}}\right|$

$E = \dfrac{Gm}{r2} = \dfrac{G}{r2} \times 4{πρ}_{0} \left(\dfrac{r3}{3} - \dfrac{r5}{5R^{2}}\right)

$E = 4{πGρ}_{0} \left(\dfrac{r}{3} - \dfrac{r3}{5R^{2}}\right)$

$E$~is maximum when~$\dfrac{dE}{dt} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{dE}{dr} = 4{πGρ}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{3r^{2}}{5R^{2}}\right) = 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{5}{3}R$

${E}_\max = 4{πGρ}_{0} \times \dfrac{5R}{3} \left[\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{5} \times \dfrac{5}{9}\right]

${E}_\max = $\dfrac{8\sqrt{5}}{27}{πGρ}_{0}$R

$

questions.q: Two identical particles each of mass $m$~go round a circle of radius $a$& under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The angular speed of each particle will be :&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The gravitational force& \left({F}_{G}\right)$ between the particles is given by

$\begin{cases}{F}_{G} & = & \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{\left(2a\right)2} \\ & = & \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4a^{2}} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The centripetal force~ \left({F}_{C}\right)~of each particle can be written as

${F}_{C} = m{ω}^{2}a . . . \left($2\right)$

Under balanced condition, equate equation (1) and equation (2) and simplify to obtain the angular speed of each particle.

$\begin{cases}m{ω}^{2}a \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{4a^{2}}\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } {ω}^{2} = \dfrac{Gm}{4a^{3}}\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{Gm}{4a^{3}}}\end{cases}$

questions.q: A body is moving in a low circular orbit about a planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$. The radius of the orbit can be taken to be $R$ itself. Then the ratio of the speed of this body in the orbit to the escape velocity from the planet is:&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The orbital velocity of the body in an orbit of the radius& $R$~is~${v}_{o} = \sqrt{\dfrac{Gm}{R}}$

The escape velocity from the surface is~${v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{R}}$

Ratio,~$\dfrac{v0}{ve} = \dfrac{\dfrac{Gm}{R}}{\dfrac{2Gm}{R}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The variation of acceleration due to gravity \left(g\right)$~with distance \left(r\right)$ from the center of the earth is correctly represented by

questions.solution:
We know that the gravitational field strength varies according to the variation of the distance of an object& from the centre of the earth.

So, gravitational field strength inside the earth varies as,

$g = \dfrac{GMr}{R3}$~if $0 \le r \le R$.

So,~$g ∝ r$.

At the surface, it is maximum,~$g = \dfrac{GM}{R2}$.

Outside the earth, it varies as,~$g ∝ \dfrac{1}{r2}$~for~$( r \ge R )$.

So, this is the possible graph,
